name: glyph_strip
description: Cut a crop that holds ONE line of text into its glyphs, count them, write one crop per glyph and a strip with index numbers, and count the readings a confusable character leaves open. A survey of ink, not a reader: this tool names no character. RULES (they are in every answer and in every refusal too): (1) Text read from a picture is a reading with an error rate. A reading with a confusable character at a position that matters (' or `, l or I or 1, O or 0) is recorded at MEDIUM confidence as a candidate set, never as one string: give the reading and the uncertain positions, and cite candidate_set_size and the candidates file. (2) The count is the number of separate ink runs along the line. It is the number of characters only when no two characters touch and no character is drawn as two strokes side by side: check wide and narrow_pairs, and look at the strip (every glyph has its index). (3) Give `uncertain` as positions with their alternatives ([{"at": 4, "among": "lI"}], positions from 0, spaces counted): the set is the product of the alternatives. Without `uncertain`, every character of the reading that is in a confusable class is uncertain. (4) The reading, the OCR text and the candidates are evidence text and can be a password or a key: they go to files, never into the answer. When the line is a credential, run the job with secret_output: true and cite the file. WHAT IT MEASURES: the crop (a PNG by a reader of its own; a JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP or TIFF picture only where Pillow imports, Pillow being given these formats alone) is thresholded (Otsu), the ink is taken as the minority colour (polarity says which), and every run of columns that hold ink is one glyph: count is the number of those runs, specks of a single pixel left out (specks_ignored). Each glyph has its box (x, y, width, height), its distance from the line's top and bottom (a mark that sits high or low), a crop (glyph-NNN.png, enlarged four times, or two or one times where four would pass 4,000,000 pixels: crop_scale) and a place in strip.png, where every glyph is enlarged at its own height in the line with its index (from 1) under it. spaces_after lists the glyphs followed by a gap wider than the others; wide lists runs that may be two touching characters (wider than 1.8 times the line's usual glyph, its median width or its median height where that is smaller, and than 1.3 times their own height); narrow_pairs lists neighbours that may be one character drawn as two strokes; same_shape_groups lists glyphs that are the same drawing (same size, at most one pixel in sixteen different); ink_bands above 2 says the crop holds more than one line. THE CANDIDATE SET: with reading (the line as you read it) every uncertain position has its alternatives and the set is their product (candidate_set_size); uncertain names the positions, each with among (the characters that glyph could be), or without among the built-in class of the reading's character (' `; l I 1 |; o O 0; s S 5; z Z 2; c C; v V; w W; x X; u U; k K; p P; 8 B; 6 G; 9 g q; . ,; : ;; - _; classes replaces the table); without uncertain every character of the reading that is in a class is uncertain. Two uncertain positions whose glyphs are the same drawing, that have the same alternatives AND that the reading gives the same character are tied (positions_tied) and counted once (an assumption where a font draws two alternatives alike); a pair that is the same drawing but read as two characters is not tied and is named (same_drawing_read_apart), so the reading itself is always in the set; positions are matched to glyphs only when the reading has as many characters besides spaces as the line has ink runs (else glyphs_not_matched says so and nothing is tied). The set is written to candidates.txt, a candidate a line, the reading itself first (first_line_is_the_reading checks it), at most max_candidates (a larger set is counted exactly, written in part, and the answer is partial). The answer says record_as: a candidate set at medium confidence, never one string. A SECOND READER: when tesseract is on PATH it is run as one line (--psm 7) on the crop as this tool decoded it (its first frame, grey, written as a PNG of the tool's own and removed after), never on the file itself, but only while at least 2 seconds of the tool's clock are left (else ocr says it was not run and the answer is partial, as it is when the engine is cut at its clock), and readers says which reader read what: the OCR engine the text (in ocr.txt), this tool the count, the caller the reading; what the engine writes is read up to 64 KiB (more is not read, and ocr says so). The OCR text's length is not printed: readers says only whether its characters besides spaces are as many as the ink runs (agrees_with_count). reading_against_ocr names a file (reading_against_ocr.tsv, mode 0600) with a row for each of the first 400 positions whatever the two lengths (whether the texts differ there, a position past either text differing, and whether it was marked uncertain) and a last row that says whether the two texts have the same length: the positions and the length follow the OCR text, so they are in the file, not in the answer, and the file's size says nothing of them. When tesseract is not there, ocr says so (available false) and nothing else changes; ocr: none skips it. NOT IN THE ANSWER: the reading, the OCR text, where the two differ, and the candidates (they are evidence text and can be a credential): they are files, mode 0600, in a new directory under $OUT (outside a job, under work/<agent>/tool-output). This tool does not declare secret output: when the line is a credential, run the job with secret_output: true. It does NOT: recognise a character, split characters that touch, join a character drawn in two strokes, straighten a slanted or curved line, or read more than one line. Status: complete when the whole picture was read and everything asked for was written; partial when the candidate set was cut, a file could not be written, the clock ran out, the OCR program asked for made no reading (an exit code, a signal, a cut, an output that is no text), the picture is cut or corrupt and Pillow read it all the same (picture_damaged: the built-in reader's finding on a PNG, the image data of every PNG Pillow is given measured as Pillow reads it (an interlaced one, one whose rows pass 256 MiB, one whose header chunk is longer than 13 bytes), or the tool's own walk of a JPEG's Huffman-coded data, which tells a JPEG cut short and given its end marker back, or of a TIFF's first page, its strips or tiles of JPEG data walked the same way and its uncompressed ones held to the bytes their rows need; a JPEG the walk does not take, arithmetic or lossless coding, old-style JPEG in a TIFF or past its time share, is jpeg_data_not_walked, partial too; a TIFF page passes only when its shape is one the walk takes: no tag named twice in its directory, strip or tile tags but not both, and uncompressed, JPEG of one plane (each strip's or tile's frame must be its size: a smaller one, whose missing rows libtiff leaves unwritten, is picture_damaged) or LZW, Deflate or PackBits in grey, RGB or palette (Pillow reads these strip by strip and libtiff fails the read on data that does not decode); every other page (CCITT, old-style JPEG, YCbCr read through libtiff's RGBA interface, any other codec, a directory the walk cannot follow) is jpeg_data_not_walked. Whatever the format, the decoding child's standard error is read (its first 64 KiB kept): a line libtiff, libjpeg or zlib print there while a frame is decoded (a note on a tag libtiff does not know aside) makes the picture picture_damaged. A known limit: WebP, BMP or uncompressed TIFF data whose tail is zeroed decodes as zeros without a word and is not told from a whole picture), more than 50 pairs of positions are the same drawing read apart (the first 50 are listed, same_drawing_read_apart_total counts them), or the OCR program left a process behind (program_group; on a host that cannot adopt orphans, such as macOS, a call that ran the OCR program is partial for that reason alone); failed for a picture that cannot be read. Every count of what was not read or not judged is printed in not_read_or_judged (zeros included), and the status is derived from that one list: any count above zero is partial. A character in among or classes that is a control character or a lone surrogate is refused. With a reading, a crop with no ink still has its candidate set written. Bounds: a crop of up to 6,000,000 pixels, at most 2,000 high and 50,000 wide (a picture past either is refused by its header, before a row of it is decoded: crop the line first), its first frame (a picture with more makes the answer partial, and frames_not_read says so), 400 glyphs, a reading of 400 characters, 200,000 candidates written; Pillow never runs in the tool's own process: a child is forked for the picture and killed (SIGKILL) when the tool's clock runs out, with its address space bounded on Linux (1 GiB more than it was forked with) and its CPU time by the clock, and a JPEG of more than 256 scans (start-of-scan markers; a picture has one, a progressive one about ten) is refused before it is handed over; the clock is read while the built-in reader walks the chunks (every 1024) and the rows, while the line is cut, the glyphs compared, the ties sought, the strip and the crops drawn and encoded, and the candidates written. Measured with Python 3.12 on an Apple M-series host: a 420 x 60 crop of 13 glyphs with a reading and tesseract 5.5 in 0.2 s. A stop signal ends it with one JSON answer (failed, interrupted), exit 128 + the signal; the OCR program is ended with it and a file that was begun is removed.

image.description: The crop: a picture that holds one line of text and little else (a path)

reading.description: The line as you read it (1 to 400 characters). With it the candidate set is counted and written. It is recorded in the trace as every argument is: for a credential, run the job with secret_output: true

uncertain.description: The positions of the reading you cannot tell (from 0, spaces counted): [{"at": 4, "among": "lI"}, {"at": 9, "among": "'`"}], or bare numbers to take each position's built-in class. Left out: every character of the reading that is in a class

classes.description: Replace the table of look-alikes: a list of strings, each one class (["'`", "lI1|", "O0"]), no character in two classes

max_candidates.description: The most candidates written (default 4096, at most 200000); the set's size is always counted exactly

ocr.description: auto (default: run tesseract as a second reader when it is on PATH) or none

reader.description: auto (default: the built-in PNG reader, Pillow for the rest) or builtin (never Pillow)

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 50, 5 to 55; the manifest's timeout is 60)
